Write "Not known yet" under a heading when the description and the codebase pass give nothing; never invent a fact. The exception is ## Priority, ## Fix approach and ## Test plan: fill them at every depth from the codebase pass, never write "Not known yet" there, and state any assumption in the section (rules in refs/create.md). -->

## Feature Summary

Thank you, Ryan, for the issue watcher and the standing coordinator (PR #707, merged). This issue asks how an issue should move between Research, Spec, Plan and Debug through the watcher, what Pipeline Full should mean, and whether a build step should exist.

## Problem Statement

Clay and a research run checked 18 possible gaps in that design. The list is IronClaude issue #761 (potential gaps to check against existing work). This issue is the part about how an issue moves through stages. All file and line facts below were checked on master at commit afb3ccf29 and verified against `origin/master` at that same commit. Each problem is a question for the owner, not a verdict.

### Problem 1: an issue does not move between stages through the watcher

The Project Status field (Research, Spec, Plan, Debug) picks the stage command. Today one claim runs one stage and the issue ends at In review. We found no way to go on to the next stage through the watcher.

- A watcher store entry in state `claimed` or `pending` is skipped as `already_dispatched` before any GitHub read (`src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/cycle.py:981-982`).
- Only an entry in state `abandoned` or `unknown` can be reset (`src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/record.py:448` and `:714`). So moving the Status back cannot start a second run.
- All four Status pipelines end at In review (`src/superclaude/cli/issue_pipeline/complete.py:55`, the table `END_STATUS`). The design says this is on purpose (`docs/designs/issue-watcher-status-pipelines.md:15`).
- Four places still tell a person that moving the Status back to an allowed value starts a relaunch: `src/superclaude/cli/issue_pipeline/templates/worker-brief.txt:17`, `src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md:297` (last sentence), and `docs/designs/issue-watcher-status-pipelines.md:65` and `:79`. By the three facts above that sentence is not true for a claimed issue. No issue tracks fixing it.
- No document, issue or pull request designs a chain from Research to Spec to Plan. We searched issues, PRs #707 and #729 and the two merged planning branches.

Why it matters: a person who reads those four sentences will move the Status back and wait for a run that never starts.

### Problem 2: what Pipeline Full means is described three different ways

- The `/sc:issue` command text says `full` also implements, with no commit and no push, and `full` with `--submit` also commits, pushes and opens a PR (`src/superclaude/commands/issue.md`, the Usage paragraph and the `--pipeline` row).
- The watcher design table says Full is the stage command plus one local commit of the report, and Full Submit adds the push and the PR (`docs/designs/issue-watcher-status-pipelines.md:19`).
- The launch prompt for Full says: make no commit (`src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/templates/launch-prompt.md:27-28`).
- With `--stage`, the claim step says step 1 is only the stage command, not the recommended chain, and that it never runs `/sc:implement` or `/task` (`src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/refs/claim.md:80`). No watcher path runs `/sc:implement`.
- Every level above None is switched off today: `GOVERNED_LEVELS_ALLOWED = False` (`src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/launch.py:48`), and such an issue ends `level_gated` (`src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/cycle.py:1029-1036`). Issue #450 (roll out the watcher, closed 2026-11-24) confirms the gate is closed.
- "Only the stage command" is prose in the skill, not code. The template keeps a step 2 slot (`src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/templates/next-steps.md:12`), the script `src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/scripts/orca_worktree.py prompt` never reads `next-steps.md`, and the tests check only the rendered launch prompt (`tests/skills/test_issue_protocol.py:343-388`).
- UNVERIFIED: what a real stage claim writes into `next-steps.md`. One check settles it: run one `--pipeline none --stage research` claim on a throwaway issue and read its `next-steps.md`.
- UNVERIFIED: the wording of the Pipeline field's option descriptions on the Project board itself (not read). One check settles it: read the field's options on the Project.

Why it matters: someone who picks Full on the board may expect a built result, a local commit, or only a report. Clay's intent is that the owner verifies Full end to end on a real issue before anyone relies on it.

### Problem 3: the launch prompt contradicts itself between Worktree and Plan

At Worktree level the prompt says a person approves only by running the printed implement command in the session, a prompt starting `/sc:implement`, `/sc:task` or `/task` (`src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/templates/launch-prompt.md:25`). For `--stage plan` the same file says never run `/sc:implement` or `/task` for this stage (`:45`). So at Worktree with stage Plan, the approval route the first block names is the one the second block forbids. No issue, PR or test names this conflict.

## User Story

As a person moving an issue through the Project board, I want the Status and Pipeline fields to have one clear meaning, so that I know what runs next and do not wait for a run that cannot start.

## Proposed Solution

The owner is asked to answer these four questions before implementation:

(a) Should the Status chain Research to Spec to Plan through the watcher, or should it only show progress while the Pipeline field carries the work?

(b) Should a build step through the watcher exist at all? Issue #733 (unattended mode for `/sc:implement`) lists "an implement row in the issue pipeline's worker brief" as out of scope (its item B8), so nothing plans it today. Issue #689 (plan everything at creation, claim goes straight to workflow and implement) was closed as not planned on 2026-11-23.

(c) Can a code check make sure a stage claim holds only the stage command, so it stops being prose only?

(d) Can the false relaunch sentence (four places, Problem 1) and the Worktree and Plan wording conflict (Problem 3) be fixed in text? Which of the three descriptions of Full (Problem 2) is the intended one? Clay offers to write the text fixes once (d) is answered.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The owner answers (a) to (d) in this issue. The answers state whether stage chaining and a build step are wanted, whether a code check is wanted, and which meaning of Full is intended.
- [ ] The false relaunch sentence is removed or made true in all four places: `src/superclaude/cli/issue_pipeline/templates/worker-brief.txt`, `src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`, and both passages in `docs/designs/issue-watcher-status-pipelines.md`.
- [ ] One description of Pipeline Full is chosen. The issue command, watcher design, claim instructions and launch prompt match it. Any difference between a manual claim and a watcher stage claim is stated plainly.
- [ ] The Worktree and Plan wording conflict is removed from `src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/templates/launch-prompt.md`. A reviewer can follow the Plan instructions without being told both to run and not run an implement command.
- [ ] If the answer to (c) is yes, a test fails when a stage claim holds more than its allowed stage command or stage route. The check covers the claim's `next-steps.md`, not only the rendered launch prompt. Spec's documented brainstorm and design route remains covered.
- [ ] The two UNVERIFIED items in Problem 2 are settled by their named checks and the results are recorded here, or remain explicitly marked UNVERIFIED. Full is not presented as verified end to end until the owner has checked it on a real issue within the existing gate rules.

## Out of Scope

- Opening the ship gate. That is an owner decision and depends on issue #442 (live observations of the launch-level guard), issue #678 (a bare `claude <prompt>` command runs a turn outside the limits) and issue #722 (the owner and the AI helpers share one GitHub login, so the system cannot tell who approved).
- The unattended implement mode itself (issue #733) and the unattended review loop (issue #734).
- Replacing the merged watcher. It is the design (owner ruling R38).

## Components Affected (from `/sc:analyze`)

- Watcher dispatch and reset: `src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/cycle.py`, `src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/record.py`, `src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/launch.py`.
- Stage completion: `src/superclaude/cli/issue_pipeline/complete.py`.
- Worker instructions: `src/superclaude/cli/issue_pipeline/templates/worker-brief.txt`, `src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`.
- Watcher design: `docs/designs/issue-watcher-status-pipelines.md`.
- Issue command: `src/superclaude/commands/issue.md`.
- Claim instructions and templates: `src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/refs/claim.md`, `src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/templates/next-steps.md`, `src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/templates/launch-prompt.md`.
- Prompt rendering: `src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/scripts/orca_worktree.py`.
- Tests: `tests/skills/test_issue_protocol.py`, `tests/issue_pipeline/test_brief.py`, `tests/skills/test_worker_contract.py`.

## Related Issues/PRs

- #733: unattended mode for `/sc:implement`.
- #734: unattended mode for the plan review loop.
- #442: live observations of the launch-level guard.
- #678: launch-level guard, a bare `claude <prompt>` runs a turn outside the limits.
- #722: shared GitHub login, how to tell who approved.
- #689: closed, not planned: claim goes straight to workflow and implement.
- #450: closed 2026-11-24: roll out the watcher; the ship gate is closed.
- #761: the list of potential gaps this issue comes from.
- PR #707: the merged issue watcher and standing coordinator.

## Priority

High: a documented command or gate fails, because the documented step of moving the Status back to relaunch does not work for a claimed issue. Priority requested by Clay.

## Fix approach

Repo: IronbellyOrg/IronClaude. Base branch: master.

Commands, in order: after the owner answers (a) to (d), run `/sc:workflow`, then `/sc:implement` with the resulting plan path, then `/sc:pr-submit --monitor 3`.

Steps, in order:

- Step 1: Record the owner's answers in this issue. Use `docs/designs/issue-watcher-status-pipelines.md` to state the intended stage flow and meaning of each Pipeline value. Keep the ship gate closed. Do not treat this issue as permission to add chaining or a build step without those answers.
- Step 2: Correct the four relaunch passages in `src/superclaude/cli/issue_pipeline/templates/worker-brief.txt`, `src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md` and `docs/designs/issue-watcher-status-pipelines.md`. Check the wording against `src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/cycle.py`, `src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/record.py` and `src/superclaude/cli/issue_pipeline/complete.py`. Change behavior only if the owner's answer calls for it.
- Step 3: Align `src/superclaude/commands/issue.md`, `src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/refs/claim.md`, `src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/templates/next-steps.md`, `src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/templates/launch-prompt.md` and the watcher design with the chosen meaning of Full. Remove the Worktree and Plan conflict without adding permission to implement during a Plan stage.
- Step 4: If (c) is yes, add the agreed stage-claim check at the claim output boundary. Review `src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/scripts/orca_worktree.py` as the prompt-rendering boundary and cover the generated `next-steps.md` in `tests/skills/test_issue_protocol.py`. Keep the allowed Spec route explicit. The existing prompt renderer alone does not read or check that file.
- Step 5: Update `tests/issue_pipeline/test_brief.py` and `tests/skills/test_worker_contract.py` to pin the corrected instructions. Run the regression gate and regenerate the development copies with `make sync-dev` before checking sync. Leave `src/superclaude/cli/issue_watch/launch.py` and its ship gate unchanged unless a separate owner decision authorizes that work.

## Test plan

- Tests to add or change: in `tests/skills/test_issue_protocol.py`, add coverage of a stage claim's generated `next-steps.md` if (c) is yes. Include a failing case with an extra implementation step and passing cases for Research, Spec, Plan and Debug, including the allowed Spec route. Keep the existing rendered-prompt checks and add a Worktree with Plan case that pins the corrected approval and stop wording.
- Tests to add or change: update `tests/issue_pipeline/test_brief.py::test_the_brief_says_a_relaunch_needs_the_status_moved_back` and `tests/skills/test_worker_contract.py::test_the_duties_name_the_status_to_command_table_and_the_brief_at_level_none_only` so they pin the owner's corrected relaunch instructions rather than the current sentence.
- Regression gate: run `uv run pytest`, `make lint` and `make verify-sync`. Run `make sync-dev` before the sync check when installed primitives change. All three checks must pass.
- How a reviewer verifies: read the owner's answers to (a) to (d), compare all four relaunch passages with the watcher skip and reset rules, and compare the Full descriptions across the command, claim instructions, prompt and design table. Render the Worktree with Plan prompt and confirm its instructions no longer conflict. If (c) is yes, demonstrate that an extra implementation step makes the new stage-claim test fail. Read the saved `next-steps.md` from the throwaway `--pipeline none --stage research` check and the Project field options to settle the two UNVERIFIED items. Any real-issue Full check remains subject to the existing ship gate and its separate prerequisites.

## Backlog review, 2026-11-24

Read-only review of this issue against the current source and its history (automated analysis, then an independent evidence review that passed).

- **State:** still-relevant
- **Complexity / size:** Medium / M
- **Priority:** P2

#### Concrete next steps

1. Owner answers (a) to (d) in #772 in chat; the agent records them (owner never writes a file). Without the answers nothing below should change behaviour.
2. After answer (d): fix the four relaunch passages (worker-brief.txt:17, WORKER-CONTRACT.md:297, design :65 and :79) and update `tests/issue_pipeline/test_brief.py:242` and `tests/skills/test_worker_contract.py::test_the_duties_name_the_status_to_command_table_and_the_brief_at_level_none_only` to pin the new wording. Edit `src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md` at its source, then run `make sync-dev`.
3. Remove the Worktree-with-Plan conflict in `launch-prompt.md:25` versus `:45` without allowing implement in a Plan stage; add a rendered-prompt test for that case.
4. Pick one meaning of Full and align `commands/issue.md:16`, `refs/claim.md`, `templates/launch-prompt.md` and the design table.
5. If (c) is yes, add a `next-steps.md` check at the claim output boundary with a failing-case test; keep the Spec brainstorm-then-design route allowed.
6. Settle the two UNVERIFIED Problem 2 items only through the owner's real-issue check, within the existing gate.
7. Run `uv run pytest`, `make lint`, `make verify-sync` (not run here; this task forbids uv).

#### Dependencies

- Needs: the owner's answers to (a) to (d) in #772. The ship gate (out of scope) depends on #442, #678 and #722, all OPEN.
- Blocks: nothing hard. Any plan to chain stages or add a build step through the watcher depends on these answers; #733 (unattended `/sc:implement`, OPEN) lists an implement row in the issue pipeline brief as out of scope.

#### Related issues

#761 (OPEN, list of potential gaps this issue comes from), #733 (OPEN), #734 (OPEN), #442 (OPEN), #678 (OPEN), #722 (OPEN), #689 (CLOSED, not planned per the issue body; state CLOSED confirmed, reason not re-read), #450 (CLOSED).

#### Related PRs

#707 (MERGED, the watcher and standing coordinator), #729 (MERGED, records R38: the merged watcher is the design), #591 (MERGED, coordinator handoff, Plan B), #584 (MERGED, approval core). No open PR addresses #772.

_Limits: items marked UNVERIFIED in the text could not be checked in this read-only review. Nothing was changed on this issue other than this comment and its field values._

title: [FEATURE] Stage flow through the watcher: moving between Research, Spec, Plan and Debug, what Pipeline Full means, and a build step
